{{Short description|Mathematical concept in differential geometry}}
{{technical|date=November 2011}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''polar action''' is a proper and [[isometry|isometric]] [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] of a [[Lie group]] ''G'' on a complete [[Riemannian manifold]] ''M'' for which there exists a complete [[submanifold]] Σ that meets all the [[orbit (group theory)|orbit]]s and meets them always orthogonally; such a submanifold is called a '''section'''. A section is necessarily [[totally geodesic]]. If the sections of a polar action are [[flat manifold|flat]] with respect to the induced metric, then the action is called '''hyperpolar'''.

In the case of linear orthogonal actions on [[Euclidean space]]s, polar actions are called '''polar [[group representation|representation]]s'''. The isotropy representations of Riemannian [[symmetric space]]s are basic examples of polar representations. Conversely, Dadok has classified polar representations of compact Lie groups on Euclidean spaces, and it follows from his classification that such a representation has the same orbits as the isotropy representation of a symmetric space.

==References==
*Berndt, J; Olmos, C; Console, S. (2003). "Submanifolds and holonomy", Chapman & Hall/CRC, Research Notes in Mathematics, 434, {{isbn|1-58488-371-5}}
